#### Android SDK

The Log Service Android SDK enables data collection on the Android platform, allowing you to write log data.

#### C SDK

The Log Service C SDK is designed for log ingestion from various platforms, including devices that use MIPS chips or run OpenWrt systems. The C SDK uses libcurl for networking and the apr/apr-util libraries for memory management and cross-platform support. To get started, compile the SDK from source. The C SDK also includes the Producer Library and the Producer Lite Library, which provide a simple, high-performance, and low-resource solution for cross-platform log collection. For more details, see the following GitHub projects: C Producer Library (recommended for server-side use) C Producer Lite Library (recommended for IoT and smart devices)

#### SDK for Go

Log Service provides developers with the SDK for Go to simplify the use of Log Service. The Log Service SDK for Go allows developers to perform the following operations: Write and consume data in batches. Use keywords to query indexes. Manage Logtail configurations and machine groups. You can download the SDK for Go from the following GitHub URL: https://github.com/aliyun/aliyun-log-go-sdk. For information about the usage instructions and sample code, see README.

#### Node.js SDK

Cloud Defined Storage Log Service SDK for Node.js allows developers to use Log Service by using Node.js programs. This topic describes how to use Log Service SDK for Node.js to write log data to Log Service.

**Procedure**

1. Create an Apsara Stack tenant account.
2. Obtain an Apsara Stack AccessKey pair.
The AccessKey pair will be used in the following steps and must be kept confidential. For information about how to use the AccessKey pair in Log Service SDK for Node.js, see Basic configurations.
3. Create a project.
i. Use the Node.js web framework Express to create a project. For more information, see installing. ii. Install morgan. iii. Create an app.js file in the project. The app.js file contains the following code:

```
var express = require('express') var morgan = require('morgan') var app = express() const logger = morgan(function (tokens, req, res) {
  return [
    tokens.method(req, res),
    tokens.url(req, res),
    tokens.status(req, res),
    tokens.res(req, res, 'content-length'), '-',
    tokens['response-time'](req, res), 'ms'
  ].join(' ')
}) app.use(logger) app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('Hello World!')) app.listen(3000, () => console.log('Example app listening on port 3000!'))
```

iv. Run the **node app.js** command to start the project. Visit `http://localhost:3000` . Then, access logs are generated.
4. Write logs to Log Service.

### API Reference

#### Overview

In addition to the Apsara Stack console, Simple Log Service provides an API to programmatically write and query log data, and manage projects and Logstores.

| Config | ListConfig, CreateConfig, DeleteConfig, GetConfig, and UpdateConfig |
|---|---|
|  | GetAppliedMachineGroups (get the machine groups a config is applied to) |
| Machine group | ListMachineGroup, CreateMachineGroup, DeleteMachineGroup, GetMachineGroup, and UpdateMachineGroup |
|  | ApplyConfigToMachineGroup and RemoveConfigFromMachineGroup |
|  | GetAppliedConfigs (get the list of applied configs) |
| Logstore | ListLogstore, CreateLogstore, DeleteLogstore, GetLogstore, and UpdateLogstore |
|  | GetLogs (query logs) and GetHistograms (query log distribution) |
| Index | GetIndex, CreateIndex, DeleteIndex, and UpdateIndex |
| Shard | ListShards, SplitShard, and MergeShards |
|  | PostLog (writes logs) |
|  | GetCursor (gets a cursor for a specific log position) |
|  | PullLogs (consumes logs) |
| Consumer group | CreateConsumerGroup, DeleteConsumerGroup, ListConsumerGroup, and UpdateConsumerGroup |
|  | HeartBeat (sends a heartbeat), GetCheckPoint, and UpdateCheckPoint |

Cloud Defined Storage You can use the API to: Collect logs based on Logtail configurations and Logtail machine groups. Create Logstores, write logs to them, and read logs from them.

**Note**

The API is RESTful. All API requests require authentication. For details on request signing, see request signature.

#### Common request headers

The Log Service API is a RESTful API based on the HTTP protocol. The Log Service API supports a set of common request headers that can be used in all API requests. Each Log Service API request must provide a common request header. The following table describes the fields of the common request headers.

| Header field | Typ e | Description |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accept | Strin g | The type of the response that the client expects Log Service to return. Two response types are supported: application/json and application/x-protobuf. This field is optional and valid for only GET requests. The specific value is subject to the definition of each API. |  |  |
| Accept- Encoding | Strin g | The compression algorithm that the client expects Log Service to return. LZ4 and DEFLATE are supported. The value can also be an empty string, indicating that no compression is performed. This field is optional and valid only for GET requests. The specific value is subject to the definition of each API. |  |  |
| Authorizatio n | Strin g | The signature content. For more information, see Request signatures. |  |  |
| Content- Length | Num eric valu e | The length of the HTTP request body defined in RFC 2616. If the request does not have a body, this field is not required. |  |  |
| Content- MD5 | Strin g | The uppercase string that is generated after the request body is calculated based on the MD5 algorithm. If the request does not have a body, this field is not required. |  |  |
| Content- Type | Strin g | The type of the HTTP request body defined in RFC 2616. Log Service API requests support only two types: application and x-protobuf. If the request does not have a body, this field is not required. The specific value is subject to the definition of each API. |  |  |
| Date | Strin g | The time when the request is sent. Only the RFC 822 format is supported. The GMT standard time is used. The formatted string is %a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT, for example, Mon, 3 Jan 2010 08:33:47 GMT. |  |  |
| Host | Strin g | The complete hostname of the HTTP request. The value does not include protocol headers such as http:// . Example: big- game.regionid.example.com . |  |  |
|  |  |  | big- |  |
| x-log- apiversion | Strin g | The API version. The current version is 0.6.0. |  |  |
| x-log- bodyrawsiz e | Num eric valu e | The initial size of the request body. If the request does not have a body, the value is 0. If the request body is compressed, the value is the size of the initial data before the compression. Valid values: 0 to 3 × 1024 × 1024. This field is optional and only required when the request body is compressed. |  |  |
| x-log- compressty pe | Strin g | The compression type of the API request body. LZ4 and DEFLATE that are defined in RFC 1951 are supported. If you want to use the ZLIB compression type, see RFC 1950. If the request body is not compressed, this field is not required. |  |  |
| x-log-date | Strin g | The time when the request is sent. The time format is the same as that of the Date field. This field is optional. If a request contains this field, the value of this field replaces the value of the Date field for the request verification performed by Log Service. The Date field must be provided regardless of whether a request has an x-log-date field. |  |  |
| x-log- signaturem ethod | Strin g | The signature calculation method. Set the value to hmac-sha1 . |  |  |

Cloud Defined Storage

**Note**

The maximum difference between the time represented by the Date field of a request and the time when Log Service receives the request is 15 minutes. If the difference exceeds 15 minutes, Log Service rejects the request. If an x-log-date field is specified in the request, the time difference is calculated based on the value of the x-log-date field. If the compression algorithm is specified in x-log-compresstype of a request, the raw data must be compressed and then placed into the HTTP request body. The values of Content-Length and Content-MD5 fields are calculated based on the compressed HTTP body. The value of the Date field cannot be specified for the HTTP requests sent by some platforms. As a result, no correct value of the Date field is available to calculate the request signature. In this case, you must specify an x-log-date field and use the value of this field to calculate the request signature. After Log Service receives an API request, it checks whether the request contains an x-log-date field. If yes, Log Service uses the value of the x-log-date field for signature verification. If no, Log Service uses the value of the standard HTTP field Date for signature verification.

#### Request signatures

To ensure the security of log data, each HTTP request of a Simple Log Service API operation must pass security verification. Simple Log Service uses the asymmetric encryption algorithm to verify API requests based on Apsara Stack AccessKey pairs. The following process shows the security verification process of an API request: Cloud Defined Storage
1. The client generates a string-to-sign based on the HTTP headers and body of an API
request.
2. The client uses an AccessKey pair that consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret
to sign the string-to-sign. A digital signature is generated for this API request.
3. The client sends the signed API request to the server.
4. The server receives the request and then repeats Steps 1 and 2.

**Note**

The server retrieves the AccessKey pair from the backend to calculate the signature and generate the expected digital signature for this request.
5. The server compares the expected digital signature with the digital signature sent from the
client. If they are the same, the request passes security verification. Otherwise, the request is rejected. The following figure shows the security verification process. Figure 1. Security verification process The security verification process can also be used to perform the following operations: Identify who sends the API request. A user must specify an AccessKey pair to generate the digital signature for an API request. Simple Log Service uses the AccessKey pair to identify the user and implement access control. Check whether the API request is tampered with during transmission. The server calculates the digital signature of an API request and compares the digital signature with the signature sent from the client. If the request is tampered with during transmission, the two signatures are different and the verification fails.

**Sign an API request**

To pass the security verification for an API request, you must sign the API request on the client by using a digital signature. You must also use the Authorization header to transmit the digital signature of the API request over the network. The Authorization header is specified in the following format: In the preceding format, the value of the Authorization header contains the AccessKey ID. The AccessKey secret is used to construct the signature. The following procedure describes how to construct the signature:
1. Prepare an AccessKey pair.
To generate a digital signature for an API request, you must use an AccessKey pair. The AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret.

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| VERB | The HTTP method that is used to send the request. | PUT, GET, and POST |
| CONTENT-MD5 | The MD5 hash value of the HTTP request body. The value contains only uppercase letters. | 875264590688CA6171F6228AF5BBB3 D2 |
| CONTENT-TYPE | The type of the HTTP request body. | application/x-protobuf |
| DATE | The timestamp of the request. Specify the timestamp in the time format that is defined in Request for Comments (RFC) 1123. The timestamp must be in UTC. | Mon, 3 Jan 2010 08:33:47 GMT |
| CanonicalizedLOGH eaders | The string constructed by the custom headers in the HTTP request. The custom headers are prefixed with x-log and x- acs . | x-log-apiversion:0.6.0\nx-log- bodyrawsize:50\nx-log- signaturemethod:hmac-sha1 |
| CanonicalizedResou rce | The string that is constructed by using the HTTP request resources. | /logstores/app log _ |

| x- |  |
|---|---|

|  | acs |
|---|---|

Cloud Defined Storage
2. Generate a string-to-sign for the API request
The string-to-sign of a Simple Log Service API request is constructed based on the method, headers, and body of the HTTP request. The string-to-sign is generated by using the following formula:

```
SignString = VERB + "\n"
             + CONTENT-MD5 + "\n"
             + CONTENT-TYPE + "\n"
             + DATE + "\n"
             + CanonicalizedLOGHeaders + "\n"
             + CanonicalizedResource
```

In the preceding formula, \n indicates the line feed escape character and the plus sign ( + ) indicates the string concatenation operator. The following table describes the other parameters. Table 1. Parameter of a string-to-sign If an HTTP request does not have a request body, the values of the CONTENT-MD5 and CONTENT-TYPE headers are empty strings. In this case, the string-to-sign is generated by using the following formula:

```
SignString = VERB + "\n"
             + "\n"
             + "\n"
             + DATE + "\n"
             + CanonicalizedLOGHeaders + "\n"
             + CanonicalizedResource
```

The `x-log-date` custom header is used in Simple Log Service API operations. For more information, see Common request headers. If you specify this header in an API request, the value of this header replaces the value of the DATE header when you calculate a signature. Cloud Defined Storage The following procedure describes how to construct the CanonicalizedLOGHeaders string: i. Convert the names of all HTTP request headers that are prefixed by `x-log` and `x-` `acs` into lowercase letters. ii. Sort all custom request headers that are obtained in the previous step in alphabetical order. iii. Delete all spaces on each side of the delimiter between each header and the value of the header. iv. Separate all headers and values with the \n delimiter to obtain the CanonicalizedLOGHeader string. The following procedure describes how to construct the CanonicalizedResource string: i. Set the CanonicalizedResource string to an empty string (""). ii. Enter the Simple Log Service resources that you want to access, such as /logstores/logstorename. If `logstorename` does not exist, use an empty string. iii. If the request contains a query string ( `QUERY_STRING` ), add a question mark ( ? ) and the query string to the end of the CanonicalizedResource string. In the request, `QUERY_STRING` is the string generated after the request parameters are sorted in alphabetical order in the URL. Equal signs ( = ) are used between the names and values of parameters to form a string. The name-value pairs are sorted in alphabetical order and connected with ampersands ( & ) to form a string. The following formula shows how to construct a query string:

```
QUERY_STRING = "KEY1=VALUE1" + "&" + "KEY2=VALUE2"
```

3. Generate a digital signature for an API request
API operations of Simple Log Service support only the `HMAC-SHA1` digital signature algorithm, which is also the default signature algorithm. Use the algorithm in the following format:

```
Signature = base64(hmac-sha1(UTF8-Encoding-Of(SignString),AccessKeySecret))
```

The HMAC-SHA1 method defined in RFC 2104 is used as the signature method. The AccessKey secret in the preceding formula must match the AccessKey ID in the Authorization header. Otherwise, the request cannot pass the security verification of the server. After the digital signature is generated, enter the signature into the Authorization header. Then, specify the header in the HTTP request and send the request. The following two examples demonstrate how to sign an API request. In the examples, the following AccessKey pair is used to sign the API requests:

```
AccessKeyId = "<yourAccessKeyId>" AccessKeySecret = "<yourAccessKeySecret>"
```

Example 1: To list all Logstores of a project named ali-test-project, send the following GET request:

```
Mon, 09 Nov 2015 06:11:16 GMT x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1
```

Cloud Defined Storage The following string is the string-to-sign that is generated for the API request:

```
GET\n\n\nMon, 09 Nov 2015 06:11:16 GMT\nx-log-apiversion:0.6.0\nx-logsignaturemethod:hmac-sha1\n/logstores?logstoreName=&offset=0&size=1000
```

A GET request does not have an HTTP body. The values of the CONTENT-MD5 and CONTENT-TYPE headers are empty strings. The following string is the digital signature calculated by using the specified AccessKey secret:

```
jEYOTCJs2e88o+y5F4/S5IsnBJQ=
```

The following request is a signed HTTP request:

```
Mon, 09 Nov 2015 06:11:16 GMT x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 Authorization: LOG <yourAccessKeyId>:<yourSignature>
```

Example 2: Write the following log entry to the test-logstore Logstore in the ali-test-project project:

```json
topic="" time=1447048976 source="10.10.10.1" "TestKey": "TestContent"
```

To do this, send the following POST request:

```xml
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2015 06:03:03 GMT x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 Content-MD5: 1DD45FA4A70A9300CC9FE7305AF2C494 Content-Length: 52 x-log-apiversion:0.6.0 x-log-bodyrawsize:50 x-log-compresstype:lz4 x-log-signaturemethod:hmac-sha1 <The log is serialized to byte streams in the ProtoBuffer format.>
```

In this HTTP request, the log is first serialized to byte streams in the ProtoBuffer format and then used as the request body. For more information, see Data encoding. In this case, the value of the Content-Type header is application/x-protobuf. The value of the Content-MD5 header is the MD5 hash value of the HTTP request body. The following string is the stringto-sign that is generated for the API request:

```
POST\n1DD45FA4A70A9300CC9FE7305AF2C494\napplication/x-protobuf\nMon, 09 Nov 2015 06:0 3:03 GMT\nx-log-apiversion:0.6.0\nx-log-bodyrawsize:50\nx-log-compresstype:lz4\nx-log -signaturemethod:hmac-sha1\n/logstores/test-logstore
```

The following string is the digital signature that is calculated by using the specified AccessKey secret:

```
XWLGYHGg2F2hcfxWxMLiNkGki6g=
```

#### Common error codes

When an API request error occurs, Log Service returns an error message, including the HTTP status code and the specific error details in the response body. The error details in the response body are formatted as follows:

```json
{ "errorCode" : <ErrorCode>, "errorMessage" : <ErrorMessage> }
```

Some of the error messages that may be returned by Log Service apply to most APIs and are defined as common error codes. The other error messages apply only to some APIs and are defined as special error codes. The unique error codes of an API are described in the relevant API reference.

| 400 | InvalidBodyRawSiz e | x-log-bodyrawsize is invalid. | The error message returned because the x-log-bodyrawsize value is invalid. |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | InvalidCompressTy pe | x-log-compresstype {type} is unsupported. | The error message returned because the compression type specified in the x-log- compresstype parameter is not supported. |
| 400 | MissingHost | Host does not exist in http header. | The error message returned because the Host field does not exist in the HTTP request header. |
| 400 | MissingDate | Date does not exist in http header. | The error message returned because the Data field does not exist in the HTTP request header. |
| 400 | InvalidDateFormat | Date {date} must follow RFC822. | The error message returned because the value of the Date field in the request header does not comply with the RFC 822 standard. |
| 400 | MissingAPIVersion | x-log-apiversion does not exist in http header. | The error message returned because the x-log-apiversion field does not exist in the HTTP request header. |
| 400 | InvalidAPIVersion | x-log-apiversion {version} is unsupported. | The error message returned because the value of the x-log- apiversion field in the HTTP request header is not supported. |
| 400 | MissAccessKeyId | x-log-accesskeyid does not exist in header. | The error message returned because no AccessKey ID exists in the Authorization header field. |
| 401 | Unauthorized | The AccessKeyId is unauthorized. | The error message returned because the specified AccessKey ID is unauthorized. |
| 400 | MissingSignatureM ethod | x-log-signaturemethod does not exist in http header. | The error message returned because the x-log- signaturemethod field does not exist in the HTTP request header. |
| 400 | InvalidSignatureMe thod | signature method {method} is unsupported. | The error message returned because the signature method specified in the x-log- signaturemethod header field is not supported. |
| 400 | RequestTimeTooSk ewed | Request time exceeds server time more than 15 minutes. | The error message returned because the request sending time is more than 15 minutes before or after the current server time. |

Cloud Defined Storage

| 404 | ProjectNotExist | Project {name} does not exist. | The error message returned because the specified project does not exist. |
|---|---|---|---|
| 401 | SignatureNotMatch | Signature {signature} is not matched. | The error message returned because the digital signature of the request does not match the signature computed in Log Service. |
| 403 | WriteQuotaExceed | Write quota is exceeded. | The error message returned because the log write quota is exceeded. |

##### GetProjectLogs

Queries logs in a project by using an SQL statement.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| query | string | Yes | The SQL statement that is used for the query. |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| x-log-progress | String | The status of the query results. Valid values: Incomplete and Complete. |
| x-log-count | Integer | The total number of logs in the query results. |
| x-log-processed-rows | Integer | The number of rows that were processed in the query. |
| x-log-elapsed- millisecond | Integer | The number of milliseconds that were consumed by the query. |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| time __ __ | Integer | The log timestamp. The timestamp follows the UNIX time format. It is the number of seconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 Thursday, January 1, 1970. |

Cloud Defined Storage

**q**

**y**

The following example shows the request syntax of the GetProjectLogs operation:

```
GET /logs query=SELECT avg(latency) as avg_latency FROM where __date__ >'2017-09-01 00 :00:00' and __date__ < '2017-09-02 00:00:00' Date: Wed, 3 Sept. 2014 08:33:46 GMT Host: big-game.cn-hangzhou.log.aliyuncs.com x-log-bodyrawsize: 0 x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1
```

**Request elements**

The GetProjectLogs operation does not have operation-specific request headers. For information about the common request headers of Log Service API operations, see Common request headers. Request parameters

**Response elements**

For information about the common response headers of Log Service API operations, see Common response headers. The following table describes the response headers that are specific to this operation. Response parameters The response body of the GetProjectLogs operation is an array. Each element in the array is a log. The following table describes the response parameters.

| source __ __ | String | The log source that was specified when logs were written. |
|---|---|---|
| [content] | Key-value pair | The original content of logs. |

| HTTP status code | Error code | Error message | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | ParameterInvalid | parameter is invalid | The error message returned because the specified parameter in the request is invalid. |

Cloud Defined Storage

**Additional considerations**

The query statement that is used in this API operation is a standard SQL statement. You must specify a project in the domain name of the request. You must specify a Logstore in the FROM clause of the query statement. A Logstore can be regarded as an SQL table. You must specify a time range in the SQL statement by using the __date__ parameter (timestamp) or __time__ parameter (UNIX timestamp). If the number of logs in a Logstore significantly changes, Log Service cannot predict the number of times you must call this API operation to obtain complete results. In this case, you must check the value of the x-log-progress parameter in the returned results of each request. You can also call this API operation again to obtain the complete results based on the value of this parameter.

**Note**

Each time you call this operation, the same number of charge units (CUs) are consumed. In addition to Common error codes, the API operation may also return the following operationspecific error codes. In this example, the logs whose topic is groupA are queried in a Logstore named app_log. The Logstore belongs to a project named big-game in the China (Hangzhou) region. The time range is from 00:00:00 UTC, September 1, 2014 to 22:00:00 UTC, September 1, 2014, and the keyword is "error". The query starts from the start of the time range. A maximum of 20 logs can be returned. Sample requests

```
GET /logs/?query=SELECT * FROM <logStoreName> where __line__ = 'abc' and __date__ >'2 017-09-01 00:00:00' and __date__ < '2017-09-02 00:00:00'&line=20&offset=0 HTTP/1.1 Date: Wed, 3 Sept. 2014 08:33:46 GMT Host: big-game.cn-hangzhou.log.aliyuncs.com x-log-bodyrawsize: 0 x-log-apiversion: 0.4.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1
```

In the sample response, the value of the x-log-progress parameter is Complete. This value indicates that all logs are queried and the returned results are complete. Two logs meet the specified query conditions. The logs are displayed as the value of the logs parameter. If the value of the x-log-progress parameter in the response is Incomplete, you must repeat the request to obtain complete query results.

#### Logstore operations

##### CreateLogstore

Creates a Logstore.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| logstoreName | string | Yes | The name of the Logstore. The name must be unique within the project. |
| ttl | integer | Yes | The data retention period of the Logstore, in days. Valid values: 1 to 3600. |
| shardCount | integer | Yes | The number of shards in the Logstore. Valid values: 1 to 100. |
| enable tracking _ | boolean | No | Enables or disables web tracking. Default value: false. |
| autoSplit | boolean | No | Enables or disables auto split for shards. Default value: false. |
| maxSplitShard | integer | No | The maximum number of shards for auto split. Valid values: 1 to 64. The default value is 64. This parameter is required if autoSplit is set to true. |

Cloud Defined Storage

```json
Date: <GMT Date> Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 {
    "logstoreName" : <logStoreName>,
    "ttl": <ttl>,
    "shardCount": <shardCount>,
    "autoSplit": <autoSplit>,
}
```

**Request elements**

This operation uses no specific request headers. For more information about the common request headers for Log Service APIs, see common request headers. Request parameters

**Response elements**

This operation uses no specific response headers. For more information about the common response headers for Log Service APIs, see common response headers. Response elements A successful request returns an HTTP 200 status code. In addition to the common error codes, this operation can return the following operationspecific error codes.

| HTTP status code | ErrorCode | ErrorMessage |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | LogstoreAlreadyExist | Logstore {logstoreName} already exists |
| 500 | InternalServerError | Specified server error message |
| 400 | LogstoreInfoInvalid | Logstore info is invalid |
| 400 | ProjectQuotaExceed | project quota exceeded |

##### CreateSubstore

The CreateSubstore API works in conjunction with the CreateLogstore API to create a Metricstore. For more information about using CreateLogstore, see CreateLogstore.

| Property name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectName | string | Yes | The name of the project. |
| MetricStoreName | string | Yes | The name of the Metricstore. |
| subStore | class | Yes | The full-text index. |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | string | Yes | The name of the subStore. The default value is prom. |

Cloud Defined Storage

**Note**

To create a Metricstore, perform the following steps:
1. Call the CreateLogstore API and set the TelemetryType parameter to Metrics to create a
Metricstore.
2. Call the CreateSubstore API to complete the configuration of the Metricstore.
The syntax of the API request is as follows:

```json
Date: <GMT Date> Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 {
    "projectName" : <projectName>,
    "MetricStoreName": <metricStoreName>,
    "subStore": <subStore>
}
```

**Request elements**

The CreateSubstore API does not have specific request headers. For information about the common request headers of Log Service API, see Common request headers. Request parameters subStore configuration parameters

| Ttl | integer | Yes | The data retention period. Unit: days. Valid values: 1 to 3600. |
|---|---|---|---|
| TimeIndex | integer | Yes | The expiration time of the time index. Unit: days. |
| SortedKeyCount | integer | Yes | The metrics of the Metrics. |
| Keys | arrays | Yes | name : The name of the Metric. __ __ Example: nginx ingress controller response size _ _ _ _ labels : The label information in the following __ __ format: {key}#$#{value}\|{key}#$#{value}\| {key}#$#{value}. Example: app#$#ingress- nginx\|controller class#$#nginx\|controller na _ _ mespace#$#kube- system\|controller pod#$#nginx-ingress- _ controller-589877c6b7-hw9cj time nano : The timestamp in nanoseconds. __ _ __ 1585727297293000000 value : The value. __ __ 36.0 For more information, see the Time series data (Metric) section in the Terms chapter of the Quick Start section in the Simple Log Service User Guide. |

Cloud Defined Storage

**Response elements**

The CreateSubstore API does not have specific response headers. For information about the common response headers of Log Service API, see Common response headers. Response elements The HTTP status code 200 is returned.

Cloud Defined Storage

```java
import com.aliyun.openservices.log.Client; import com.aliyun.openservices.log.common.LogStore; import com.aliyun.openservices.log.common.SubStore; import com.aliyun.openservices.log.common.SubStoreKey; import com.aliyun.openservices.log.exception.LogException; import com.aliyun.openservices.loghub.client.exceptions.LogHubClientWorkerException; import java.util.Arrays; public class SimpleTest {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws LogHubClientWorkerException,
InterruptedException, LogException {
        String endpoint = "***";
        String ak = "***";
        String sk = "***";
        String projectName = "sls-metric-test";
        String MetricStoreName = "sls_metric_test";
        Client client = new Client(endpoint, ak, sk);

        logStore.setTelemetryType("Metrics");

        SubStore subStore = new SubStore();

        subStore.setTimeIndex(2);

        SubStoreKey subStoreKey4 = new SubStoreKey("__value__", "double");

subStoreKey4));
        // Create a MetricStore
        client.createSubStore(projectName, MetricStoreName, subStore);

}
```

```python
from aliyun.log import LogClient, LogStore, SubStore, SubStoreKey from aliyun.log.exception import LogException def main():
    endpoint = "***"
    ak = "***"
    sk = "***"
    project_name = "sls-metric-test"
    metric_store_name = "sls_metric_test"
    # Create a LogClient
    client = LogClient(endpoint, ak, sk)
    # Create a LogStore
    log_store = LogStore(metric_store_name, 1, 2)
    # Create a SubStore
    sub_store = SubStore()
    sub_store.set_name("prom")
    sub_store.set_ttl(1)
    sub_store.set_time_index(2)
    sub_store.set_sorted_key_count(2)
    key1 = SubStoreKey("__name__", "text")
    key2 = SubStoreKey("__labels__", "text")
    key3 = SubStoreKey("__time_nano__", "long")
    key4 = SubStoreKey("__value__", "double")
    sub_store.set_keys([key1, key2, key3, key4])
    # Create MetricStore
    try:
        client.create_sub_store(project_name, metric_store_name, sub_store)
    except LogException as e:
        print(f"LogException: {e}")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

##### GetCursor

Queries a cursor based on a point in time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| shard | String | Yes | The name of the shard. |
| type | String | Yes | This parameter must be set to cursor. |
| from | String | Yes | The time that is used to query a cursor. Set the value to a Unix timestamp or a string such as begin or end . |

Cloud Defined Storage You can use a cursor to obtain the location of a specific log. The following figure shows the relationships among a cursor, project, Logstore, and shard. Each project has multiple Logstores. Each Logstore has multiple shards. You can use a cursor to obtain the location of a specific log. The request syntax of the GetCursor API operation is as follows:

```
GET /logstores/ay42/shards/2? type=cursor&from=1402341900 HTTP/1.1 Date: <GMT Date> Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0
```

**Request elements**

The GetCursor API operation does not have special request headers. For information about common request headers of Log Service API operations, see Common request headers. Request parameters You can use the from parameter to locate the logs within the lifecycle of a shard in a Logstore. If the lifecycle of the Logstore is `[begin_time, end_time)` and the from parameter is set to from_time, the response is returned as follows:

| Note The lifecycle of a Logstore is specified by the ttl parameter of the Logstore. For example, the current time is 2018-11-11 09:00:00 and the ttl parameter is set to 5. The time interval of consumable data in each shard is [2018-11-05 09:00:00, 2018-11- 11 09:00:00) . The server time is used. |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | [2018-11-05 09:00:00, 2018-11- |  |

| HTTP status code | Error code | Error message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | LogStoreNotExist | Logstore {Name} does not exist |
| 400 | ParameterInvalid | Parameter From is not valid |
| 400 | ShardNotExist | Shard {ShardID} does not exist |
| 500 | InternalServerError | Specified Server Error Message |
| 400 | LogStoreWithoutShard | the logstore has no shard |

Cloud Defined Storage from_time ≤ begin_time or from_time = "begin" : A cursor is returned. The cursor corresponds to the log whose timestamp is begin_time. from_time ≥ end_time or from_time = "end" : A cursor is returned. The cursor corresponds to the next log to be written at the current time (No data exists in the current cursor location). `from_time > begin_time and from_time < end_time` : A cursor is returned. The cursor corresponds to the first packet that Log Service receives later than or at from_time.

**Response elements**

The GetCursor API operation does not have special response headers. For information about common response headers of Log Service API operations, see Common response headers. Response parameters

```json

    "cursor": "MTQ0NzI5OTYwNjg5NjYzMjM1Ng=="
```
```json
}
```

##### PullLogs

Pulls logs from a Logstore. You must specify a shard when you call this API operation. Only Protocol Buffer log data can be pulled from a Logstore. For more information, see Protocol Buffer format. In scenarios that involve the Storm architecture, election and collaborative consumption can be performed through LoghubClientLib.

```
GET /logstores/ay42/shards/0? type=logs&cursor=MTQ0NzMyOTQwMTEwMjEzMDkwNA==&count=100 H TTP/1.1 Accept: application/x-protobuf Accept-Encoding: lz4 Date: <GMT Date> Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1
```

##### PostLog

Writes log data to a Logstore. Only Protocol Buffer log data can be written to a Logstore. For more information, see Protocol Buffer format.

**Note**

Log data is written in the form of log groups. Log data can be written to a Logstore in either of the following modes: LoadBalance: In this mode, Log Service automatically writes logs to all writable shards in a Logstore. This mode provides high availability (SLA: 99.95%) in data writes. It applies to scenarios where data writes and reads are irrelevant to shards, for example, where ordering is not considered.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time | Integer | Yes | The time when the log was generated. |
| Contents | List | Yes, this field must contain at least one element. | The list of log fields. For information about the field elements, see the Content field table. |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Key | String | Yes | The name of the custom key. |
| Value | String | Yes | The value of the custom key. |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Key | String | Yes | The name of the custom key. |
| Value | String | Yes | The value of the custom key. |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Logs | List | Yes | A list of logs. For information about the field elements, see the Log field table. |
| Topic | String | Yes | A user-defined field in a log. This field identifies a group of logs. |

Cloud Defined Storage KeyHash: The key field is added to the URL parameter. This determines which shard to store the log data. This field is optional. If you do not specify this field, Log Service automatically writes log data in the LoadBalance mode. For example, Log Service can hash an instance as a producer to a fixed shard based on the name of the instance. This ensures that data is written and consumed by using a strict order in the shard. The key is included only in the MD5 value range of a shard at a time even when the shard is merged or split. For more information, see Shards.

**Protocol Buffer log data**

The following table describes the fields of Protocol Buffer log data. For more information, see Data model and Data encoding. Log Content LogTag LogGroup

| Source | String | Yes | The source of the log, for example, the IP address of the machine where the log is generated. |
|---|---|---|---|
| LogTags | List | Yes | The list of log tags. For information about the field elements, see the LogTags field table. |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| logstorename | String | Yes | The name of the Logstore to which logs are written. |

Cloud Defined Storage LoadBalance mode

```xml
POST /logstores/<logstorename>/shards/lb HTTP/1.1 Content-Type: application/x-protobuf Content-Length: <Content Length> Content-MD5: <Content MD5> Date: <GMT Date> Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-bodyrawsize: <BodyRawSize> x-log-compresstype: lz4 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 <Compressed log data in the Protocol Buffer format>
```

KeyHash mode

```xml
POST /logstores/<logstorename>/shards/route? key=14d2f850ad6ea48e46e4547edbbb27e0 Content-Type: application/x-protobuf Content-Length: <Content Length> Content-MD5: <Content MD5> Date: <GMT Date> Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-bodyrawsize: <BodyRawSize> x-log-compresstype: lz4 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 <Compressed log data in the Protocol Buffer format>
```

**Request elements**

For information about common request headers of Log Service API operations, see Common request headers. Request parameters

| HTTP status code | Error code | Error message | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | PostBodyInvalid | Protobuffer content cannot be parsed. | The error message returned because the logs in the Protocol Buffer format cannot be parsed. |
| 400 | InvalidTimestamp | Invalid timestamps are in logs. | The error message returned because the logs contain invalid timestamps. |
| 400 | InvalidEncoding | Non-UTF8 characters are in logs. | The error message returned because the logs contain non-UTF-8 characters. |
| 400 | InvalidKey | Invalid keys are in logs. | The error message returned because the logs contain invalid keys. |
| 400 | PostBodyTooLarge | Logs must be less than or equal to 3 MB and 4096 entries. | The error message returned because the size of logs is greater than 3 MB or the number of logs exceeds 4,096. |
| 400 | PostBodyUncompressE rror | Failed to decompress logs. | The error message returned because the logs fail to be decompressed. |

Cloud Defined Storage

**Response elements**

The PutLogs API operation does not have special response headers. For information about common response headers of Log Service API operations, see Common response headers. Response parameters No response element is returned after the request succeeds.

**Additional considerations**

You can call the PutLogs API operation to write a maximum of 3 MB log group data or 4,096 logs each time. The size of values in each log cannot be greater than 1 MB. If these limits are exceeded, the request will fail and no log data will be written. Log Service checks the format of log data written by the PutLogs API operation. If a log does not meet the format requirements, the request will fail and no log data will be written. In addition to Common error codes, the API operation may also return the following special error codes.

| 499 | PostBodyInvalid | The post data time is out of range | The error message returned because the log timestamp is not within the valid range: [-7 × 24 hours, + 15 minutes]. |
|---|---|---|---|

##### GetLogs

The GetLogs operation queries logs from a specified logstore. Use parameters to query for logs that meet specific conditions.

**How it works**

After a log is written to a logstore, the latency before it can be queried by Log Service operations like GetHistograms and GetLogs varies by log type. Log Service classifies logs into two types based on their timestamp:
**Real-time data**: The log's timestamp is within the range of (-180 seconds, +900 seconds]
relative to the server's current time. For example, if a log has a timestamp of UTC 2014-09- 25 12:03:00 and the server receives it at UTC 2014-09-25 12:05:00, the log is processed as real-time data. This is typical.
**Historical data**: The log's timestamp is within the range of [-7 days, -180 seconds) relative
to the server's current time. For example, if a log has a timestamp of UTC 2014-09-25 12:00:00 and the server receives it at UTC 2014-09-25 12:05:00, the log is processed as historical data. This typically occurs when backfilling data. For real-time data, the maximum query latency is 3 seconds. In 99.9% of cases, the latency is under 1 second. The request syntax for the GetLogs operation is as follows:

| project | String | Yes | ali-test-project | The name of the project. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| logstore | String | Yes | example- logstore | The logstore to query. |

Cloud Defined Storage

```xml
GET /logstores/<logstorename>?type=log&topic=<logtopic>&from=<starttime>&to= <endtime>&query=<querystring>&line=<linenum>&offset=<startindex>&reverse=<ture|false> H TTP/1.1 Date: <GMT Date> Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-bodyrawsize: 0 x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1
```

##### GetHistograms

The GetHistograms API queries the distribution of logs in a specified Logstore within a Project. You can also specify parameters to query the distribution of only the logs that meet specific conditions. The latency from when a log is written to a Logstore until it becomes queryable through the GetHistograms and GetLogs APIs varies by log type. Log Service classifies logs into the following two types based on the log timestamp:
**real-time data**: The log timestamp is within the range of (-180 seconds, +900 seconds]
relative to the server's current time. For example, if a log's timestamp is UTC 2014-09-25 12:03:00 and the server receives it at UTC 2014-09-25 12:05:00, Log Service processes the log as real-time data. The latency for real-time data to become queryable is 3 seconds.
**historical data**: The log timestamp is within the range of [-7 days, -180 seconds) relative
to the server's current time. For example, if a log's timestamp is UTC 2014-09-25 12:00:00 and the server receives it at UTC 2014-09-25 12:05:00, Log Service processes it as historical data. This typically occurs when backfilling data. The request syntax for the GetHistograms API is as follows.

```
GET /logstores/<logstorename>?type=histogram&topic=<logtopic>&from=<starttime>&to=<endt ime>&query=<querystring> HTTP/1.1 Date: <GMT Date> Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-bodyrawsize: 0 x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1
```

**Request elements**

This API has no specific request headers. For common Log Service API request headers, see common request headers. Request parameters

| to | int | Yes | The end of the time range to query, specified as a Unix timestamp in seconds. |
|---|---|---|---|
| topic | string | No | The topic of the logs to query. |
| query | string | No | The query expression used to filter logs. For detailed syntax, see the sections of the User Guide : Query and Analysis > Query Syntax and Functions > Query Syntax. |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| progress | string | The query status. Valid values are Incomplete and Complete . |
| count | int | The total log count in the current result set. |
| histograms | array | An array of objects representing the log distribution across the sub-intervals. |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| from | int | The start of the sub-interval, specified as a Unix timestamp in seconds. |
| to | int | The end of the sub-interval, specified as a Unix timestamp in seconds. |
| count | int | The number of logs matching the query in this sub-interval. |
| progress | string | Indicates whether the query results for this sub- interval are complete. Valid values are Incomplete and Complete . |

Cloud Defined Storage

**Response elements**

This API returns no specific response headers. For common Log Service API response headers, see common response headers. Response parameters A successful request returns a response body showing the distribution of matching logs over the specified time range. The response divides this range into uniform sub-intervals and provides the log count for each. Each object in the `histograms` array has the following structure. All time ranges in this API, including the `from` and `to` request parameters and the subintervals in the response, are left-inclusive and right-exclusive, denoted as `[start, end)` . If the values of `from` and `to` are the same, the time range is invalid and the API returns an error. The service consistently divides the time range into the same sub-intervals for identical requests.

| HTTP status code | Error code | Error message | Description |

| 404 | LogStoreNotExist | logstore {Name} does not exist | The specified Logstore does not exist. |
| 400 | InvalidTimeRange | request time range is invalid | The specified time range is invalid. |
| 400 | InvalidQueryString | query string is invalid | The specified query is invalid. |

Cloud Defined Storage For large queries, Log Service cannot predict how many requests are required to retrieve the complete result set. You must check the `progress` value in each response to determine whether to repeat the request for the remaining results.

##### GetIndex

Queries the indexes of a Logstore. The request syntax of the GetIndex API operation is as follows:

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| logstoreName | String | Yes | The name of the Logstore. |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| index mode _ | String | The type of the indexes. |
| keys | Dictionary | The key-value index, where the key refers to the field name and the value refers to the field value. |
| line | object | The full-text index. |
| storage | String | The storage type. The default value is pg, which refers to PostgreSQL. |
| ttl | Integer | The time to live (TTL) of the index file. Valid values: 7, 30, and 90. Unit: days. |
| lastModifyTime | Integer | The time when the indexes were last modified. The value is a Unix timestamp. |

##### PutWebtracking

In standard Web Tracking, each request writes a single log. For high-volume scenarios, you can use the `PutWebtracking` API to combine multiple logs into a single request. To use this API, you must enable Web Tracking on the Logstore. This API is suitable for collecting logs from web pages and clients.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| logstoreName | string | Yes | The name of the Logstore. |
| endpoint | string | Yes | The endpoint of Log Service. For more information, see Endpoints. |
| project | string | Yes | The name of the Project. |

Cloud Defined Storage

```json
POST {project}.{endpoint}/logstores/{logstoreName}/track HTTP/1.1 x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-bodyrawsize: 1234 x-log-compresstype: gzip {
  "__topic__": "topic",
  "__source__": "source",
  "__logs__": [
    {
      "key1": "value1",
      "key2": "value2"
    },
    {
      "key1": "value1",
      "key2": "value2"
    }
```

`],`

```json
  "__tags__": {
    "tag1": "value1",
    "tag2": "value2"
  }
}
```

This operation uses the following specific request headers: x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 x-log-bodyrawsize: 1234 x-log-compresstype: gzip The first two headers are required, and the third is optional. For more information about their format and meaning, see Common request headers. Request parameters URL parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| topic __ __ | string | No | The log topic. |
| source __ __ | string | No | The log source. |
| logs __ __ | list | Yes | A list of log entries. Each element is a JSON object that represents a log. Note The log time is the time when the log arrives at the server. You do not need to specify the time __ __ field. If this field is included, the server overwrites its value. |
| tags __ __ | object | No | The log tags. |

The `PutWebtracking` operation returns only common response headers. For more information, see Common response headers. Response elements A successful request returns an empty response body. Request example

##### MetricStore HTTP API

Log Service provides Prometheus-compatible APIs to query and write time series data in MetricStore. This topic explains how to use them. The APIs provided by Prometheus are available under the /api/v1 path. MetricStore APIs follow the same convention, and their full URL is https://{project}.{slsendpoint}/prometheus/{project}/{metricstore}/api/v1/.

| {project} | Yes | The name of your Project. For more information, see CreateProject. |
|---|---|---|
| {metricstore} | Yes | The name of your MetricStore. For more information, see CreateSubstore. |

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| query | Yes | The PromQL expression. For more information, see the Introduction to time series data query and analysis section in the Log Service User Guide. |
| time | No | The evaluation time, specified as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. If omitted, it defaults to the server's current time. |
| timeout | No | The query timeout, in seconds. This parameter also supports time duration formats such as 1s , 2m , 3h , and 4d . Example: timeout=10s . For more information, see Time Durations. |
| lookback delta _ | No | Use this parameter to override the Prometheus query.lookback-delta flag for the current query only. The value must follow the Time Durations format, for example, lookback delta=1m . For more information, see _ Time Durations. This parameter specifies the maximum lookback window for finding data points during a PromQL evaluation. In the Log Service time series database, the default value is "3m". |

Cloud Defined Storage

**Important**

These APIs require Basic authentication. Set **Username** to your AccessKey ID and
**Password** to your AccessKey Secret. As a best practice, use a RAM user's AccessKey. For
more information, see Obtain an AccessKey. The RAM user requires permissions to query the specified Project. For more information, see the **Resource Access Management**
**(RAM)** section in the **Log Service User Guide**.

**Time series metric query APIs**

MetricStore provides two APIs for querying time series data: the Instant Queries API and the Range Queries API.

**Instant Queries API**

The Instant Queries API evaluates metric data at a single point in time. The following table describes the parameters. This API can return the following four result types:

**vector**

**Range Queries API**

The Range Queries API evaluates metric data at multiple points over a time range.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| query | Yes | The PromQL expression. For more information, see the Introduction to time series data query and analysis section in the Log Service User Guide. |
| start | No | The start time of the query range, specified as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. |
| end | No | The end time of the query range, specified as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. |
| step | No | The time interval between query steps, in seconds. This parameter also supports time duration formats such as 1s , 2m , 3h , and 4d . Example: step=2m . For more information, see Time Durations. |
| timeout | No | The query timeout, in seconds. This parameter also supports time duration formats such as 1s , 2m , 3h , and 4d . Example: timeout=10s . For more information, see Time Durations. |
| lookback delta _ | No | Use this parameter to override the Prometheus query.lookback-delta flag for the current query only. The value must follow the Time Durations format, for example, lookback delta=1m . For more information, see Time _ Durations. This parameter specifies the maximum lookback window for finding data points during a PromQL evaluation. In the Log Service time series database, the default value is "3m". |

Cloud Defined Storage

```
GET https://{project}.{slsendpoint}/prometheus/{project}/{metricstore}/api/v1/query_range POST https://{project}.{slsendpoint}/prometheus/{project}/{metricstore}/api/v1/query_range
```

**Metadata query APIs**

Log Service provides APIs compatible with the Prometheus metadata APIs for querying labels and series. Use these APIs to retrieve all metrics, labels, and label values within a specific time range, but they do not return timestamps or sample values.

**Query Series API**

The Query Series API returns the set of time series that match one or more selectors over a specified time range.

```
GET https://{project}.{sls-endpoint}/prometheus/{project}/{metricstore}/api/v1/series POST https://{project}.{sls-endpoint}/prometheus/{project}/{metricstore}/api/v1/series
```

The following table describes the parameters.

| start | No | The start time of the query range, as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. Defaults to 5 minutes before the current time. |
|---|---|---|
| end | No | The end time of the query range, as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. Defaults to the current time. Important Even if you specify custom values for start and end, this API only queries data from the 5-minute interval immediately preceding the end time, which is the (end - 5 minutes, end) interval. |

| (end |  |
|---|---|

|  |  | - 5 minutes, end) |
|---|---|---|

**Remote Write API**

You can ingest time series data into MetricStore by configuring the `remote_write` parameter in your Prometheus configuration file. For more information, see the **Ingest Prometheus**
**monitoring data through the remote write protocol** chapter in the **Log Service User**
**Guide**. MetricStore is compatible with the Prometheus remote write protocol. This
compatibility allows you to send data directly to the `remote_write` endpoint via HTTP requests, without needing a running Prometheus instance. Use the following endpoint to write data to MetricStore using the remote write protocol:

```
POST https://{project}.{sls-endpoint}/prometheus/{project}/{metricstore}/api/v1/write
```

The following code provides an example.

```java

 "bytes"
 "flag"
 "fmt"
 "github.com/gogo/protobuf/proto"
 "github.com/golang/snappy"
```

```
 "io/ioutil"
 "net/http"
```

The query and write APIs share the following response structure:

```json
{
  "status": "success" | "error",
  "data": <data>,
  // The following fields are returned when an error occurs during query evaluation.
  "errorType": "<string>",
  "error": "<string>",
 // Warning messages, typically returned when the query result is incomplete.
  "warnings": ["<string>"]
}
```

Cloud Defined Storage The following sections describe common errors and how to resolve them.

**Authentication failure**

This response indicates an authentication failure. Verify that your AccessKey ID and AccessKey Secret are correct.

```json
{
    "status": "error",
    "code": "401",
    "errorType": "unauthorized",
    "error": "get query instance error: {\n    \"httpCode\": 401,\n    \"errorCode\":
\"Unauthorized\",\n \"errorMessage\": \"AccessKeyId not found: xxxx\",\n \"requestID\": \"xxxx\"\n}" }
```

This error can also occur if the RAM user associated with the AccessKey lacks the necessary permissions to access the Project. Ensure the RAM user has been granted the required permissions.

```json
{
    "status": "error",
    "code": "401",

\"Unauthorized\",\n \"errorMessage\": \"AccessKeyId not found: xxxx\",\n \"requestID\": \"xxxx\"\n}" }
```

**Invalid PromQL expression**

This response indicates that the PromQL statement is invalid. Correct the expression in the
**query** parameter.

```json
--> /api/v1/query_range?query=up[2m]&start=1676700599&end=1676700999&step=60s {
    "status": "error",
    "errorType": "bad_data",
    "error": "invalid expression type \"range vector\" for range query, must be Scalar
or instant Vector" }
```

**Timeout error**

This response indicates that the query timed out. Increase the **timeout** value.

```json
{
    "status": "error",
    "errorType": "timeout",
    "error": "query timed out in expression evaluation"
}
```

**Incomplete query**

The `warnings` field in the response indicates that the query returned incomplete results. To resolve this, try reducing the query's time range. Cloud Defined Storage

##### CreateMachineGroup

| groupAttribute | object | Yes | The attribute of the machine group. Default value: null. |
| machineList | Array | Yes | The specific machine identifier, which can be an IP address or user-defined identifier. |

#### Consumer group operations

##### CreateConsumerGroup

Creates a consumer group for a specified Logstore.

```json
POST /logstores/<logstoreName>/consumergroups HTTP/1.1 x-log-bodyrawsize: 0 User-Agent: <UserAgent> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 Date: <GMT Date> Content-Type: application/json Content-MD5: F58544E4D022CC28A93D0B7CC208A5AA Content-Length: <ContentLength> {
  "consumerGroup": <consumerGroup>,
  "timeout": <timeout>,
  "order": <order>
}
```

**Request elements**

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| logstoreName | string | Yes | The name of the Logstore. |
| consumerGroup | string | Yes | The name of a consumer group must be unique in a project. |
| timeout | integer | Yes | The timeout period. If no heartbeat is received within the timeout period, the consumer will be deleted. |
| order | bool | Yes | Specifies whether to consume data in a shard in sequence. true: consumes data in a shard in sequence. After a shard is split, data in the original shard is consumed first, and then data in the two new shards is consumed at the same time. false: does not consume data in a shard in sequence. |

| HTTP status code | ErrorCode | ErrorMessage |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | ConsumerGroupAlreadyExist | consumer group already exist |
| 400 | JsonInfoInvalid | consumerGroup or timeout is of error format |
| 404 | ProjectNotExist | The Project does not exist : {Project} |
| 404 | LogStoreNotExist | logstore {logstoreName} dose not exist |
| 500 | InternalServerError | Specified Server Error Message |

Cloud Defined Storage The CreateConsumerGroup operation does not have operation-specific request headers. For more information about the common request headers of Log Service API operations, see Common request headers. Request parameters

**Response elements**

The CreateConsumerGroup operation does not have operation-specific response headers. For more information about the common response headers of Log Service API operations, see Common response headers. Response parameters The HTTP status code 200 is returned. In addition to the common error codes of Log Service API operations, this operation may also return the following special error codes. Cloud Defined Storage Sample request

```json
POST /logstores/my-logstore/consumergroups HTTP/1.1 Header: Authorization: LOG <yourAccessKeyId>:<yourSignature> x-log-bodyrawsize: 0 x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 Host: my-project.cn-shanghai.log.aliyuncs.com x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 Date: Fri, 04 May 2018 08:02:22 GMT Content-Type: application/json Content-MD5: F58544E4D022CC28A93D0B7CC208A5AA Content-Length: 65 Connection: Keep-Alive Body: {
  "consumerGroup": "consumer-group-1",
  "timeout": 300,
  "order": true
}
```

##### GetCheckPoint

Call the GetCheckPoint operation to obtain the checkpoint of a specified consumer group consuming a specific shard or all shards.

```
GET /logstores/<logstoreName>/consumergroups/<consumerGroup>?shard=<shardId> HTTP/1.1 x-log-bodyrawsize: 0 User-Agent: <UserAgent> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 Date: <GMT Date> Content-Type: application/json Connection: Keep-Alive
```

**Request elements**

The GetCheckPoint operation has no specific request headers. For more information about the common request headers of Log Service API operations, see Common request headers. Request parameters

| logstoreName | string | Yes | The name of the Logstore to which the consumer group belongs. |
|---|---|---|---|
| consumerGroup | string | Yes | The name of the consumer group. |
| shardId | integer | No | The ID of the shard. If the specified shard does not exist, an empty list is returned. If no shard is specified, the checkpoints of all shards are returned. |

| Property name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| shard | integer | The ID of the shard. |
| checkpoint | string | The value of the checkpoint. |
| updateTime | integer | The last update time of the checkpoint. |
| consumer | string | The consumer to which the shard belongs. |

| HTTP status code | ErrorCode | ErrorMessage |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | ProjectNotExist | The Project does not exist : {Project} |
| 404 | LogStoreNotExist | logstore {logstoreName} dose not exist |

Cloud Defined Storage

**Response elements**

The GetCheckPoint operation has no specific response headers. For more information about the common response headers of Log Service API operations, see Common response headers. Response parameters If the GetCheckPoint request succeeds, the response body contains the checkpoint of the shard consumed by the specified consumer group. The following table describes the format of the response body. In addition to the common error codes of Log Service API operations, this operation may also return the following special error codes.

| 404 | ConsumerGroupNotExi st | consumer group not exist |
|---|---|---|
| 500 | InternalServerError | Specified Server Error Message |

##### HeartBeat

Sends heartbeat messages to Log Service for a specified consumer.

| Property name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| logstoreName | string | Yes | The name of the Logstore, which must be unique in the project. |
| consumerGroup | string | Yes | The name of the consumer group, which must be unique in the project. |
| consumer | string | Yes | The consumer. |
| {Shard ID List} | array | Yes | The list of shard IDs that are being consumed. |

Cloud Defined Storage

```xml
POST /logstores/<logstoreName>/consumergroups/<consumerGroup>?type=heartbeat&consumer=< consumer> HTTP/1.1 x-log-bodyrawsize: 0 User-Agent: <UserAgent> x-log-apiversion: 0.6.0 Host: <Project Endpoint> x-log-signaturemethod: hmac-sha1 Date: <GMT Date> Content-Type: application/json Content-MD5: F58544E4D022CC28A93D0B7CC208A5AA Content-Length: <ContentLength> <shard ID list>
```

The HeartBeat operation does not have operation-specific request headers. For more information about the common request headers of Log Service API operations, see Common request headers. Request parameters

The HeartBeat operation does not have operation-specific response headers. For more information about the common response headers of Log Service API operations, see Common response headers. Response parameters If the HeartBeat request succeeds, the HTTP status code 200 is returned along with a list of all shard IDs that the consumer is responsible for consuming. | 404 | ConsumerGroupNotExist | consumer group not exist |

#### External store

##### Overview

When you query and analyze logs, you can associate Log Service with an external store to obtain more comprehensive results. Differences between an external store and a Logstore Scenarios Use SQL JOIN statements to query Logstores and external stores. Writes the query result from a Logstore to an external store. Storage type The available external stores include Object Storage Service (OSS) objects, local files, and ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL databases in a virtual private cloud (VPC). For more information, see **Associate Log Service with external data sources** in **Log Service User Guide**.

##### CreateExternalStore

Creates an external store. The available external stores include Object Storage Service (OSS) objects, local files, and ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL databases in a virtual private cloud (VPC). This topic describes how to modify the parameters of an ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance. For information about how to configure other external data sources, see **Associate Log Service with external data**
**sources** in **Log Service User Guide**.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| projectName | String | Yes | ali-test- project | The name of the project. |
| externalStore Name | String | Yes | rds store _ | The name of the external store. The name must be unique in a project and must be different from Logstore names. |
| storeType | String | Yes | rds-vpc | The storage type. Set the value to rds-vpc, which indicates an ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL database in a VPC. |
| vpc-id | String | No | vpc- bp1aevy8sofi 8mh1q**** | The ID of the VPC to which the ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance belongs. |

Cloud Defined Storage

#### RAM or STS

##### Overview

This topic describes how to access Log Service resources of an Apsara Stack tenant account as a Resource Access Management (RAM) user. You can access these resources only after you grant the RAM user the required permissions by using RAM. Cloud Defined Storage

**Background information**

You can create projects, Logstores, Logtail configurations, and machine groups in Log Service. By default, you have full permissions on these resources. You can manage the resources by calling the related API operations. However, if you use your Apsara Stack tenant account to create a RAM user, the RAM user has no permissions to manage your resources. To allow the RAM user to manage your resources, you must grant the required permissions to the RAM user.

**Note**

For more information about how to grant a RAM user the permissions to access Log Service resources, see **Apsara Uni-manager Management Console User**
**Guide > Enterprise > Permissions > Role Permissions**.
If you do not need to grant other users the permissions to access Log Service resources of your Apsara Stack tenant account, you can skip this section. If you skip this section, your understanding of other sections is unaffected.

**RAM policies**

You can attach the following policies to a RAM user. Then, the RAM user has the corresponding permissions on your Log Service resources. AliyunLogFullAccess If you attach this policy to a RAM user, the RAM user has full permissions to access Log Service resources of your Apsara Stack tenant account. The following example shows the policy:

```json
  {
    "Version": "1",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Action": "log:*",
        "Resource": "*",
        "Effect": "Allow"
      }
```

]

```
  }
```

AliyunLogReadOnlyAccess If you attach this policy to a RAM user, the RAM user has the read-only permissions to access Log Service resources of your Apsara Stack tenant account. The following example shows the policy:

```json
 {
    "Version": "1",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Action": [
          "log:Get*",
          "log:List*"
```

`],`

```json
        "Resource": "*",
        "Effect": "Allow"
      }
```

]

```
  }
```

Query data of a specified Logstore in the console If you attach this policy to a RAM user, the RAM user has the read-only permissions to query the data of a specified Logstore in the console. The permissions allow the RAM user to query logs, pull logs, and view the Logstore list. The following example shows the policy:

```json
  {
    "Version": "1",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Action": ["log:List*"],
        "Resource": ["acs:log:*:*:project/<Project name>/*"],
        "Effect": "Allow"
      },
      {
        "Action": ["log:Get*"],
        "Resource": ["acs:log:*:*:project/<Project name>/logstore/<Logstore name>"],
        "Effect": "Allow"
      }
```

]

```
  }
```

##### Action list

This topic describes the actions that a RAM user can perform on Log Service resources.

**Actions that a RAM user can perform on Log Service resources**

In RAM, you can authorize the RAM user to perform the following operations on Log Service resources. The operations are classified into the following types: read, write, and list. Read operations: You can read data from Log Service resources. Write operations: You can write data to Log Service resources. List operations: You can view Log Service resources.

|  | log:GetLogStoreContextLogs | Queries the contextual logs of a specified log. |
|  | log:GetLogStoreHistogram | Queries the distribution of logs in a Logstore of a project. |
|  | log:GetLogStoreLogs | Queries logs in a Logstore of a specified project. |
|  | log:ClearLogStoreStorage | Clears the data in a Logstore. |
|  | log:DeleteLogStore | Deletes a Logstore, including all shards and indexes of the Logstore. |
|  | log:PostLogStoreLogs | Writes logs to a Logstore. |
|  | log:UpdateLogStore | Updates the attributes of a Logstore. |
|  | log:ListLogStores | Queries all Logstores in a project. |
|  | log:GetCursorOrData (GetCursor, PullLogs, and GetCursorTime) | Queries a cursor based on the server time, queries logs in a specified shard based on a cursor, and queries the server time based on a cursor. |

##### Authentication rules

When a RAM user calls Log Service API operations to access the resources of an Alibaba Cloud account, Log Service authenticate the RAM user.
